newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lum Chang says not involved in APL deal.
newsitem.headline: Lum Chang says not involved in APL deal.

text.p: Lum Chang Holdings Ltd said on Monday neither it nor its related companies, including wholly-owned subsidiary Lum Chang Securities Pte Ltd (LCS), were involved in trading APL Ltd shares.
"Neither the company nor any of its related companies had at any time traded in APL shares," a company statement said.
It said its stockbroking subsidiary LCS had also confirmed that its clients, dealers and remisiers had not traded in any APL shares through LCS.

"LCS, which is a member of the Stock Exchange of Singapore, was not privy to any information on Neptune Orient Line's (NOL) acquisition of Amercian carrier APL prior to NOL's public announcement," the statement said.
"The information was made known to LCS at the same time as the public following the announcement by NOL," it said.

Raymond Lum, executive chairman of Lum Chang, has been charged with insider trading by the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The charges relate to the proposed takeover by NOL of APL.
The SEC said Lum opened a trading account on February 25 and between then and March 18 bought 190,100 APL shares for $4.4 million.
It alleged Lum made an illegal profit after APL shares rose sharply on April 14, one day after the company announced that it would be acquired by NOL for $825 million.
The Lum Chang statement said LCS executive director, Gerald Ho, Lum's nephew, had assisted his uncle in buying the shares through Morgan Stanley Asia (Singapore) Pte Ltd in his private capacity.
It added Lum still held the APL shares, which he bought as a personal investment.
